# Pass tx, ty, fx, fy to fragment shader for splatting [S1]

The claim states that tx, ty, fx, and fy are passed to the fragment shader for splatting. The evidence explicitly defines tx and ty as volume texture coordinates and fx and fy as Gaussian texture coordinates. It further explains that these coordinates are packed into vertex attributes, decompressed in the vertex shader, and used to calculate positions and apply the 2D Gaussian texture. In standard graphics pipelines for splatting, texture coordinates (tx, ty, fx, fy) are interpolated and passed from the vertex shader to the fragment shader to sample the volume and Gaussian textures during the rendering of the splats.

The claim states that while vertex memory is compressed, index buffers can still be large. The evidence supports this in two ways: 1) It explicitly details the compression of vertex memory (reducing it from 2048M to 12M bytes). 2) It mentions that 'to reduce the size of the index buffers, the size of each patch is chosen to contain no more than 65,535 vertices so that two instead of four bytes can be used as an index.' This implies that without such constraints or specific optimizations, index buffers would be larger (using 4 bytes per index), and the text acknowledges the existence and management of these index buffers in the context of the overall memory requirements.
